title: Alabama's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Alabama's 7th Congressional District is holding its regularly scheduled general election on November 3, 2026, amid a turbulent redistricting cycle. After the U.S. Supreme Court narrowed Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act in April 2026, Alabama reverted to a 2023 Republican-drawn congressional map, triggering special primary elections on August 11, 2026, for this and three other districts. Incumbent Democrat Terri Sewell, first elected in 2010 and unopposed in the Democratic special primary, seeks a ninth term representing a district that spans parts of Birmingham, the Black Belt, and western Alabama. She will face the winner of a two-candidate Republican special primary between Ammie Akin and David Perry in a district that, under the 2023 map, saw its Black voting-age population drop slightly but remains safely Democratic.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to Alabama's 7th Congressional District general election in 2026 were found as of June 2026. The special primary has not yet occurred (scheduled for August 11, 2026), and general election polling is not yet available.

candidates.name: Terri A. Sewell
candidates.summary: Terri A. Sewell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Alabama's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2010. She serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and as a Chief Deputy Whip, and is the first Black woman ever elected to Congress from Alabama. Sewell is running unopposed in the Democratic special primary on August 11, 2026, and is the presumptive Democratic nominee for the general election.

candidates.name: Ammie Akin
candidates.summary: Ammie Akin is a Republican candidate running in the August 11, 2026 special primary for Alabama's 7th Congressional District. She holds an Ed.D. and has served as a teacher, elementary administrator, assistant superintendent, and Interim Superintendent of Briarwood Christian School. Akin is also the founder of Hub in the Hills, a community organization.

candidates.summary: David Perry is a Republican candidate running in the August 11, 2026 special primary for Alabama's 7th Congressional District. He previously served as CEO of Concourse Financial Group, a subsidiary of Protective Life Insurance Company, and was the 2024 Republican nominee for Alabama's 5th District seat on the State Board of Education. Perry also serves on the board of the Alabama Trails Foundation.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific general election polling exists as of June 2026, and the Republican nominee has not yet been determined (special primary is August 11, 2026). The forecast relies entirely on structural and historical factors. The race description explicitly states the district "remains safely Democratic" under the reinstated 2023 map, despite a slight reduction in Black voting-age population. Incumbent Terri Sewell, first elected in 2010 and unopposed in the Democratic special primary, is a well-established figure serving on the House Ways and Means Committee and as Chief Deputy Whip. She has won her previous general elections by large margins (roughly 26-34 points). The Republican field consists of two first-time congressional candidates, neither of whom has held elected office, and they must first compete in a primary. Given the district's Democratic lean, Sewell's incumbency advantage, and the lack of any contrary indicators, Democrats hold an overwhelming advantage. However, absence of polling and the ongoing redistricting uncertainty keep confidence at medium rather than high.
